To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the factors influencing adoption are different in developing countries and developed countries, and that the adoption of e-government is influenced by the individual, organizational, and environmental factors.

the factors influencing adoption are: perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, perceived enjoyment, perceived security, perceived trust, social influence, perceived cost, perceived quality, perceived service, perceived compatibility and perceived self-efficacy.
the factors influencing adoption by citizens are: (1) the perceived ease of use of a system, (2) the perceived usefulness of a system, and (3) the perceived trust of the government agency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the factors that influence citizens to adopt e-government services and how these factors are related to the behavioral intention to use e-government.
the factors that influence adoption of e-government service by citizens.
identifying the factors that influence citizens’ adoption of e-government and the need to consider the context in which these services are offered.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
e-government service adoption is influenced by both 'citizen characteristics’ and ‘organizational factors’ and that these factors are interrelated.
there is no conclusive evidence that any particular factor is more influential than the others in determining citizen adoption of e-government service.
there is a need to further investigate the factors influencing adoption and use of e-government by citizens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is a need to examine e-governance adoption from an integrated approach that takes into account both the citizen's perspective as well as the organizational factors that influence adoption of e-government service.

there is a need to examine the role of citizen characteristics in e-government service adoption, and that the role of the organization should also be examined in order to gain a holistic view of e-government service adoption by citizens.
the extant literature is inadequate in understanding the adoption of e-government by citizens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
e-government adoption research needs to focus more on citizen characteristics and organizational factors.
e-government research has been largely focused on developed countries.

there is a need to develop an integrated model for e-government service adoption that incorporates both 'citizen characteristics and organizational factors' to explain the relationship that exists in the adoption of e-government service by citizens.
